title: Marden Vale Heritage Trust: archival-grade a five-scan heritage set to one duotone house look, cut out the featured portrait, and merge captioned A4 exhibition plates
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com photo-restoration brief (an individual with 'several old photo scans' to restore 'for A4 printing to mount on my wall', naming 'color fading', 'scratches or tears' and 'blurriness' as the damage). The original conceit was KILLED and is REPLACED here because the three named damages are exactly what the connector cannot do: there is no generative heal/clone/inpaint to reconstruct a torn corner or a scratch crossing photographic texture, and no sharpen tool for 'blurriness'; the killed spec's 'cure' — a solid image_fill_area over the studio backdrop and sky — is worse than the disease because those regions carry real tonal falloff, so a flat fill leaves a visible patch. The job is therefore re-cast to a connector-doable HERITAGE-PRINT PACKAGE for a fictional local-history archive, the Marden Vale Heritage Trust, preparing a wall exhibition, 'Working Lives of the Vale'. The Trust supplies five archival scans (digitized on a flatbed with a small neutral grey step-wedge laid on the platen beside each print — standard archival digitization practice), a flat wordmark scan of its emblem, a hand-authored InDesign exhibition-plate template with live merge fields plus one @-image column, and a plate-caption CSV. The Adobe chain does the real, rewarded work: bring five differently-cast, differently-exposed scans to ONE matched archival duotone house look (each neutralized to its own in-frame grey wedge, then desaturated and toned to a common warm-monochrome target at a common black point), lift the featured portrait as a clean cutout onto archival cream for the entrance panel, prep-and-vectorize the Trust emblem for the signage, and data-merge the authored template into a press-ready A4 plate run (one captioned plate per scan). No real person, place, brand, product or trademark appears; Marden Vale Heritage Trust, the exhibition, the five sitters/scenes, the catalogue references and all copy are fictional. Adobe and Freelancer.com are platform names, not brands in the scene. A4 is exact at 2480x3508 px / 300 DPI; every output px is reached by DOWNSCALE from the declared ~3600 px archival scans, never an upscale.
one_line_ask: Bring five differently-conditioned heritage scans — each carrying an in-frame neutral grey step-wedge — to ONE matched archival duotone house look at a common black point so the wall reads as a single collection, lift the featured street-scene figure as a clean cutout onto archival cream with its interior gaps preserved, clean up and vectorize the Trust emblem, then bind the authored InDesign plate template and caption sheet into a press-ready A4 exhibition run of one captioned plate per scan.
full_brief:
The Marden Vale Heritage Trust is mounting a wall exhibition, 'Working Lives of the Vale', and needs its five key photographs turned into a cohesive, gallery-quality plate set. We are NOT asking you to invent detail that isn't there — no repainting torn corners, no cloning out scratches, no faking anything our conservator is content to leave as scanned. What ruins a heritage wall is INCONSISTENCY: our five scans came off different originals in different conditions and, side by side, they currently look like five unrelated jobs. Your task is to make them read as ONE exhibition.

We digitized each print on a flatbed, and every frame includes a small neutral grey step-wedge laid on the glass beside the photograph — an honest in-frame reference we place there as standard archival practice. The five photographs are: 'The Reeve Family' (a studio portrait, 1968); 'Quarry Crew, Vale Stone Works' (1946); 'A Draper of the High Street' (a cabinet portrait, 1902); 'Market Row' (a street scene, 1931 — this is our FEATURED image, a single standing trader with a hand on his hip); and 'Canal Wharf' (1955). They reach you in varying conditions — some faded, some colour-shifted, some flat, some sitting off-square on the scanner — and it is your judgement, print by print, to diagnose what each one needs.

The house look we want for the whole set: a warm archival monochrome — a single toned duotone, deep but not blocked-up in the shadows, and above all CONSISTENT from plate to plate so the wall reads as one collection at one common black point. The bar is this: a viewer moving along the wall must not be able to tell the five began life in different conditions — no plate may sit warmer, cooler, lighter or heavier than the rest, and none may carry a leftover colour tinge into the toned result. Correct each scan on its own terms so they all converge on that one shared target. When you're done, hand us a short sheet listing, per scan, the white-balance, exposure and black-point moves you dialled and the single archival tone you settled the whole set on, so we can confirm the collection was matched to one target rather than eyeballed frame by frame.

Then three finishing pieces. FEATURED CUTOUT: from the market-row scene, lift the standing trader cleanly off his background onto our archival-cream card for the exhibition entrance panel. He stands with a hand on his hip, so there is open space under his bent arm and between his cap and his shoulder; those see-through gaps must read as clean cream, exactly like the ground around him, and must not fill in solid. EMBLEM: our Trust emblem exists only as a flat scan on off-white paper — clean it up and turn it into crisp vector art for the exhibition signage, labels and the plate headers, so it holds razor-sharp at any size. PLATES: we have hand-built the InDesign exhibition-plate template with the real placeholder fields, an image slot and an emblem slot, and we're giving you the caption sheet — bind them so every photograph gets its own A4 plate with its toned image placed, our emblem in the header, and its plate number, title, date, catalogue reference and caption set in type. Hand back one press-ready 300 DPI A4 PDF covering all five plates, one page per photograph. Set the captions verbatim from our sheet — do not rewrite our catalogue copy.

Deliverables: the five matched archival-duotone masters, the featured trader cutout on cream, the vector emblem, and the press-ready A4 exhibition-plate PDF (one captioned plate per scan).

inputs.name: reeve_family_colour_1968.png
inputs.gen_prompt: An authentic high-resolution flatbed scan (about 3600 px on the long edge) of a heavily-aged late-1960s colour studio portrait of a seated woman, photographed straight-on. Strong overall yellow-orange colour cast and faded, low-contrast tones typical of decayed C-print dye; muted washed-out skin and fabric. A small NEUTRAL GREY step-wedge strip (a short printed greyscale target) lies flat on the scanner glass just to the RIGHT of the photograph as an archival reference. Real photographic grain, soft focus. Period-correct 1960s hair, makeup and clothing, studio lighting. Documentary realism, real pores and hair strands, no CGI gloss, no modern colour.
inputs.realism_notes: SCAN 1, faded COLOUR. The yellow cast + flat faded contrast are the state the chain must FIX; do NOT pre-correct them. The in-frame neutral grey step-wedge on the RIGHT is the free neutralisation target (agent neutralises to it by eye, reports params, then crops it out). This is a COLOUR original, so the correct path is neutralise-cast -> desaturate to true mono -> tone; skipping the neutralise-and-desaturate leaves a yellow ghost in the duotone. Declared at ~3600 px so every downscale-only output (A4 placement, cream cutout, masters) stays within source resolution.

inputs.name: quarry_crew_bw_1946.png
inputs.gen_prompt: An authentic high-resolution flatbed scan (about 3600 px on the long edge) of a 1946 black-and-white silver-gelatin group photograph: eight quarry workers in flat caps and work clothes lined up in front of a stone quarry face. A genuine monochrome print, but the SCAN has introduced a faint COOL blue-grey cast and the mid-tones are slightly flat and low in contrast. A small NEUTRAL GREY step-wedge strip lies flat on the scanner glass at the LOWER edge beside the photograph as an archival reference. Real film grain, dust specks, thin uneven scan border. Documentary realism, true monochrome subject, no colour in the picture itself, no CGI smoothness.
inputs.realism_notes: SCAN 2, TRUE monochrome with a COOL scanner cast. Triage contrast with SCAN 3: this one only needs the blue-grey cast warmed back to neutral (against the wedge) plus a tonal lift before the shared tone — it must NOT be handled like the sepia cabinet portrait. The cool cast makes it the opposite-direction correction to the warm/sepia scans, so a single blanket move cannot match the set.

inputs.name: draper_cabinet_1902.png
inputs.gen_prompt: An authentic high-resolution flatbed scan (about 3600 px on the long edge) of a 1902 sepia-toned cabinet-card portrait of a standing draper in a high-collar suit beside a studio chair. The print is BROWN by original chemical toning, and the brown is UNEVEN and quite warm/heavy. Genuine period studio backdrop, real albumen/sepia texture, foxing specks at the edges, soft vintage focus. A small NEUTRAL GREY step-wedge strip lies flat on the scanner glass at the LEFT edge beside the photograph as an archival reference. Documentary realism, no CGI gloss, no modern tones.
inputs.realism_notes: SCAN 3, ALREADY-SEPIA. This is the triage trap: it looks like 'an old brown photo' but its existing warm sepia must be DESATURATED OUT to neutral BEFORE the house tone is applied, otherwise the Trust's archival tone COMPOUNDS with the residual brown and this plate lands visibly warmer/browner than the other four and breaks the wall's tone-match. Getting it wrong is invisible on this frame alone and only shows when the toned set is compared — the sanctioned failure gate. Its own grey wedge is on the LEFT.

inputs.name: market_row_1931.png
inputs.gen_prompt: An authentic high-resolution flatbed scan (about 3600 px on the long edge) of a 1931 black-and-white street photograph: a cobbled market row with stalls, and in the foreground a SINGLE standing market trader in an apron and flat cap, ONE HAND ON HIS HIP so his bent arm forms a clear triangular gap between forearm and body, the other arm at his side. The print is LOW-CONTRAST, flat and slightly muddy, mid-grey throughout with no strong blacks or clean whites. Real film grain, silver-gelatin texture, thin scan border. A small NEUTRAL GREY step-wedge strip lies flat on the scanner glass at the LOWER-RIGHT edge as an archival reference. Documentary street realism, candid, no CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SCAN 4, the FEATURED image and the hero for the cutout. Deliberately flat/low-contrast so genuine tonal-range recovery (black point + contrast) is real authored work before the shared tone. The hand-on-hip pose gives a real INTERIOR NEGATIVE-SPACE gap (arm triangle) plus the cap/shoulder gap, so the cream cutout must use remove_background({backgroundColor}) to keep those gaps cream — a select_subject->invert->fill_area knockout would brick them solid, the exact fail to avoid. Single clear standing figure so subject isolation is honest.

inputs.name: canal_wharf_1955.png
inputs.gen_prompt: An authentic high-resolution flatbed scan (about 3600 px on the long edge) of a faded 1955 colour snapshot of a canal wharf with a moored narrowboat and stacked crates. Overall faded, slightly magenta/cyan-shifted colour typical of an aged consumer C-print, flat contrast, soft focus. The photograph sits clearly CROOKED on the scanner bed (rotated about 3 degrees) with a ragged thin WHITE scan border exposed down the left and top edges. A small NEUTRAL GREY step-wedge strip lies flat on the scanner glass at the RIGHT edge as an archival reference. Real grain, documentary snapshot realism, candid amateur framing, no CGI gloss.
inputs.realism_notes: SCAN 5, faded COLOUR + CROOKED + bordered. Forces the prep-before-grade dependent chain: auto_straighten THEN crop_to_bounds must run BEFORE neutralise/desaturate/tone, or the ragged white border survives into the crop and the tilt carries into the A4 plate. Like SCAN 1 it is colour, so it also needs neutralise -> desaturate -> tone. Its grey wedge is on the RIGHT, kept until after neutralisation then cropped out.

inputs.name: marden_vale_trust_emblem_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Marden Vale Heritage Trust' emblem inked on off-white textured paper: a compact two-colour mark — a simple line-drawn mill-wheel glyph above the words MARDEN VALE HERITAGE TRUST set in a modest condensed serif, deep ink-navy lettering. Rendered as a real scan: the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the mark sits very slightly rotated on the scan bed with generous paper margin around it, edges a touch soft. Flat solid-colour art, high enough contrast that once cleaned it will vectorize to crisp paths.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat two-colour text-bearing mark on off-white — exactly the clean-edged art image_vectorize traces well AFTER prep. gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type. The off-white (not-white, not-transparent) ground plus the padding is what makes the prep-before-trace chain matter: white drop-out to transparency THEN crop_to_bounds THEN vectorize; feeding the raw scan or a selection would trace a border box or return a black silhouette.

inputs.name: marden_vale_plate_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, NOT model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 (portrait, 2480x3508 px @ 300 DPI plus bleed) exhibition plate — ONE photograph per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<plate_no>>, <<title>>, <<date>>, <<catalogue_ref>>, <<caption>>, a header image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path merge column (@emblem_image) for the agent's vector emblem, and a main image frame wired to a second @-prefixed image-path merge column (@plate_image) so the merge drops the matching toned photo into the plate. Two @-image columns are supported by document_merge_data_layout. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (fields would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields).
inputs.realism_notes: The only connector-legal way to place an image into a laid-out page is a genuine authored .indd carrying <<fields>> AND @-image columns. BOTH agent-produced images — the toned photo (@plate_image) and the vector emblem (@emblem_image) — reach the layout ONLY through a merge @-image column, never free-form placement at coordinates; the emblem repeats the same path on every row so it lands in each header. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. The layout is the client's; the distinctive quality of each finished plate (the matched archival tone, the preserved-detail image at true A4 res) is the agent's work. Row count = 5 fixes the page==row acceptance gate. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind either @image column).

inputs.name: marden_vale_plate_captions.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns plate_no,title,date,catalogue_ref,caption,@plate_image,@emblem_image holding FIVE rows, one per photograph, matching the template merge fields. Rows (fictional heritage catalogue copy): (1) plate_no 'I', title 'The Reeve Family', date '1968', catalogue_ref 'MV-0142', a two-line caption describing a family studio portrait; @plate_image resolves to the Reeve plate-placement crop. (2) plate_no 'II', title 'Quarry Crew, Vale Stone Works', date '1946', catalogue_ref 'MV-0088', caption on the quarrymen; @plate_image the quarry crop. (3) plate_no 'III', title 'A Draper of the High Street', date '1902', catalogue_ref 'MV-0011', caption on the cabinet portrait; @plate_image the draper crop. (4) plate_no 'IV', title 'Market Row', date '1931', catalogue_ref 'MV-0057', caption on the market trader; @plate_image the market-row crop. (5) plate_no 'V', title 'Canal Wharf', date '1955', catalogue_ref 'MV-0103', caption on the wharf; @plate_image the canal crop. The @emblem_image column holds the SAME agent-produced vector-emblem path on all five rows so the Trust emblem drops into every plate header through a merge @-image column (not free-form placement). Column names must exactly match the template's <<fields>> and its two @-image columns (@plate_image, @emblem_image).
inputs.realism_notes: The @plate_image column is the binding contract: each cell must point at the agent's own produced wedge-cropped plate-placement crop so document_merge_data_layout places the right photo on the right plate; the @emblem_image column repeats the agent's vector-emblem path on all five rows so the emblem reaches each plate header via a merge @-image column too. Five rows fixes page-count == row-count == 5. All copy is fictional archive catalogue text; no real person, place or institution. Text-only document_merge_data_vector cannot bind either @-image column and is the wrong tool.

outputs.name: heritage_masters_x5
outputs.spec: Five archival-duotone masters (Reeve/Quarry/Draper/Market Row/Canal), each first neutralised to its own in-frame grey step-wedge, then desaturated to true monochrome and toned to ONE shared warm-archival duotone at ONE common black point (deep but not blocked to pure black, no channel crushed to 0). These are RETAINED archival masters kept WITH their grey step-wedge IN frame at the source scan's own resolution (~3600 px long edge; no pixels added — regraded pixels only, never an upscale), sRGB PNG. The neutrality / tone-match / black-point acceptance is graded on THESE card-BEARING masters, never on a file the wedge is cropped from. Acceptance (grader-checked on the card-bearing masters): after neutralisation each frame's wedge reads neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance) and after toning every wedge value and the set black point agree across all five; the already-sepia draper master must match the others' tone, not read warmer. DELIVERABLE 1. From each master a separate wedge-cropped, downscaled plate-placement crop is derived (steps 15-19) for the @plate_image merge cell; on those delivered crops the grader checks card-EXCLUSION (no wedge present) and >=300 DPI at the A4 image frame, not neutrality.

outputs.name: market_trader_cameo_cream.png
outputs.spec: The featured market-row trader lifted off his background onto a solid archival-cream ground for the exhibition entrance panel, produced by image_remove_background({backgroundColor: archival cream}) on the toned master — the sweep/street background gone, and the interior negative space (the triangular gap under the hand-on-hip arm, the cap/shoulder gap) preserved as cream, NOT solid-filled. sRGB PNG, ~2000 px long edge (downscale-only). Acceptance: interior gaps show the cream ground, not a bricked silhouette. DELIVERABLE 2.

outputs.name: marden_vale_trust_emblem.svg
outputs.spec: Crisp vector SVG of the two-colour Marden Vale Heritage Trust emblem (mill-wheel glyph + condensed-serif wordmark), traced from the cleaned scan for exhibition signage and labels. Produced by white-drop-out to transparency -> crop-to-bounds -> vectorize (prep-before-trace), so the paths carry the mark only, no scan border box, no off-white ground. DELIVERABLE 3.

outputs.name: marden_vale_exhibition_plates_pdf
outputs.spec: One press-ready A4 (portrait, 300 DPI) PDF of the exhibition plate run — FIVE pages, ONE captioned plate per photograph — produced by merging marden_vale_plate_captions.csv into the authored marden_vale_plate_template.indd via document_merge_data_layout (one record per page) and exporting with document_render_layout. Each plate places that photo's wedge-cropped placement crop through the @plate_image column, drops the agent-produced vector emblem into the header through a SECOND @-image column (@emblem_image, the same emblem path on every row — the emblem reaches the layout only via a merge @-image column, never free-form placement), and typesets <<plate_no>>/<<title>>/<<date>>/<<catalogue_ref>>/<<caption>> verbatim. Acceptance gate: page-count == CSV row-count == 5; each placed crop renders at >=300 DPI at the A4 image frame and shows no grey wedge; captions set verbatim. DELIVERABLE 4 (the owned composed endpoint).

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: per scan, the white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure it dialled to neutralise that frame's grey wedge, the black-point/contrast move, and whether a desaturation was applied (yes for the two colour scans and the sepia cabinet portrait; the two silver-gelatin scans note residual-cast removal), PLUS the single shared archival tone (the monochromatic tint hue/strength) all five were matched to. This is the acceptance artifact that makes 'matched to one target' checkable and the divergent per-scan corrections visible; it is an APPLIED-settings log, never a measured/eyedropper readout.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: reeve_family_colour_1968.png, quarry_crew_bw_1946.png, draper_cabinet_1902.png, market_row_1931.png, canal_wharf_1955.png, marden_vale_trust_emblem_scan.png, marden_vale_plate_template.indd, marden_vale_plate_captions.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the five archival scans, the emblem scan, the authored .indd plate template and the caption CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not the difficulty.

SCAN 5 prep: level the ~3deg tilt on canal_wharf_1955 so the border crop in the next step is clean and the plate image sits square. Must precede the crop and all grading — a dependent step; grading a still-tilted, still-bordered frame carries the ragged white edge into the A4 plate.

SCAN 5 prep: crop off the ragged white scan border revealed/levelled by straightening, leaving only the photographic image area (the grey wedge is retained for now, cropped out later at resize). Consumes step 2.

SCAN 1 (faded COLOUR, yellow cast): neutralise to its in-frame grey wedge by COOLING temperature and nudging tint off yellow-green until the wedge looks neutral, lift exposure/contrast and set the house black point, and DESATURATE to true monochrome (saturation to zero). Colour must be cast-corrected BEFORE desaturating or the yellow survives as an uneven grey. The agent reasons these values by eye and records them; it does NOT read pixel values. Authored primitive grade, not a preset, not auto_tone.

SCAN 2 (TRUE B&W, cool scanner cast): WARM the temperature and correct tint to drive the grey wedge to neutral (opposite direction to the warm/sepia scans), lift the flat mid-tones and set the SAME house black point, remove any residual chroma. Triage decision: this frame needs cast-neutralisation + tonal lift only — NOT the sepia-stripping the draper needs. Records applied WB/exposure/black.

SCAN 3 (ALREADY-SEPIA cabinet portrait): the triage crux — DESATURATE the existing brown toning fully to neutral monochrome (saturation to zero) and neutralise any residual warm bias to the grey wedge, then set the SAME house black point. Only after the original sepia is removed can the shared tone land identically; skipping the desaturation compounds brown-on-brown and this plate ends warmer than the set. Records the desaturation + WB/black applied.

SCAN 4 (FEATURED, flat low-contrast B&W): recover the crushed tonal range — set a real black point and lift contrast/clarity so the muddy mid-grey scene reads with depth on a large print — neutralise to the grey wedge and remove residual chroma to match the set's monochrome base at the SAME house black point. This tonal recovery is genuine authored work, not auto_tone. Records applied contrast/black/exposure.

SCAN 5 (faded COLOUR, post-straighten/crop): neutralise the aged magenta/cyan shift to the grey wedge, lift the flat contrast to the house black point, and DESATURATE to true monochrome. Consumes the straightened+cropped step-3 output (NOT the raw upload) so the tilt/border fixes carry through. Records applied WB/exposure/black + desaturation.

Apply the SHARED archival house tone: a single chosen warm selenium-brown monochromatic tint at one chosen strength, applied to the already-neutralised, already-desaturated SCAN 1 base. Because the base is clean neutral monochrome, the tone lands as a controlled duotone with no residual colour interference — this is why the desaturate-before-tone order matters. The agent chooses the tone (authored) and applies the identical tone to all five for the match. Consumes step 4.
Apply the SAME shared archival tone (same hue + strength as step 9) to SCAN 2's neutral monochrome base, so plate II matches plate I. Consumes step 5.

Apply the SAME shared archival tone to SCAN 3's now-DESATURATED base. This is where the triage pays off: because step 6 removed the original sepia, the shared tone lands identically to the other plates instead of compounding into a browner cast. Consumes step 6.
Apply the SAME shared archival tone to SCAN 4's contrast-recovered monochrome base. This toned master is BOTH a plate image AND the source for the featured cutout. Consumes step 7.
Apply the SAME shared archival tone to SCAN 5's neutral monochrome base, matching plate V to the set. Consumes step 8.

FEATURED CUTOUT: lift the standing trader off his street background onto a solid archival-cream ground via image_remove_background({backgroundColor: archival cream}). This is the CORRECT knockout path: it isolates the figure as foreground and keeps the interior negative space — the triangular gap under the hand-on-hip arm and the cap/shoulder gap — as clean cream. Deliberately NOT select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area: fill_area solids the whole masked region and bricks those see-through gaps, the exact failure the brief warns against. Consumes the toned hero (step 12).

Derive SCAN 1's plate-placement crop: crop the grey step-wedge and scan area OUT of frame and downscale to the placement spec (~2400 px long edge, >=300 DPI at the A4 plate image frame). Downscale/reframe of existing pixels only from the ~3600 px scan — never canvas-extend, never upscale. This wedge-free crop feeds plate I's @plate_image cell; the card-BEARING toned master (step 9, reeve_toned) is retained as the Deliverable-1 archival master and is where neutrality/tone are graded. Consumes step 9.

Derive SCAN 2's wedge-free plate-placement crop (~2400 px, >=300 DPI at the frame, downscale-only); feeds plate II's @plate_image cell. The card-bearing toned master (step 10, quarry_toned) is retained for grading. Consumes step 10.

Derive SCAN 3's wedge-free plate-placement crop (~2400 px, >=300 DPI at the frame, downscale-only); feeds plate III's @plate_image cell. The card-bearing toned master (step 11, draper_toned) is retained for grading. Consumes step 11.

Derive SCAN 4's wedge-free plate-placement crop (~2400 px, >=300 DPI at the frame, downscale-only); feeds plate IV's @plate_image cell (the full scene, distinct from the cameo cutout). The card-bearing toned master (step 12, market_toned) is retained for grading. Consumes step 12.

Derive SCAN 5's wedge-free plate-placement crop (~2400 px, >=300 DPI at the frame, downscale-only); feeds plate V's @plate_image cell. Steps 15-19 produce the five wedge-cropped @plate_image placement crops the merge binds; the retained card-bearing toned masters (steps 9-13) are the heritage_masters_x5 deliverable where neutrality/tone are graded. Consumes step 13.
Trim and downscale the cream cutout to the entrance-panel spec (~2000 px long edge), keeping the figure centred and the interior cream gaps intact. Downscale-only. DELIVERABLE 2. Consumes step 14.
EMBLEM prep-before-trace (1/3): drop the off-white paper ground of the emblem scan to transparency so the mark sits clean. White drop-out, no reconstruction. Consumes the uploaded emblem scan.

EMBLEM prep-before-trace (2/3): trim the transparent emblem to its own tight bounds, removing the generous paper margin now transparent, so the trace carries only the wheel glyph + wordmark. Tracing the untrimmed frame wastes trace resolution and can leave a stray border path. Consumes step 21.

EMBLEM prep-before-trace (3/3): vectorize the cleaned, trimmed, transparent-ground emblem to crisp SVG paths for signage and the plate header. Raster-to-vector trace of a PREPARED raster (flat mark, ground knocked to transparency, cropped to bounds). DELIVERABLE 3. Consumes step 22.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: marden_vale_plate_template.indd, marden_vale_plate_captions.csv, reeve_master, quarry_master, draper_master, market_master, canal_master, marden_vale_trust_emblem_svg
connector_workflow.note: Merge the 5-row caption CSV into the authored A4 plate template: the @plate_image column resolves to the five wedge-cropped placement crops (each dropped into the plate's main image frame), the @emblem_image column resolves to the agent's vector emblem (the same path on every row, dropped into the header frame — the emblem reaches the layout ONLY through this merge @-image column, never free-form placement), and <<plate_no>>/<<title>>/<<date>>/<<catalogue_ref>>/<<caption>> typeset verbatim per row. Emits ONE plate per row -> 5 A4 pages; page==row is the acceptance gate. [T] requires the hand-authored .indd. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind either @-image column); a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind — both avoided.

Export the merged five-page document to a single press-ready A4 (300 DPI) PDF — the exhibition plate run, one captioned plate per photograph. document_render_layout exports the whole merged document (no per-record named export is attempted, which the tool cannot do). DELIVERABLE 4, the owned composed endpoint. Consumes step 24.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into five per-scan grade chains that converge on a matched archival duotone set, plus an emblem-vector tributary and a merged A4 endpoint. SCAN 5 alone takes a prep head: auto_straighten (2) -> crop_to_bounds (3) before its grade. Each scan is then neutralised+tonal+ (for the colour/sepia scans) desaturated by image_apply_adjustments with a per-scan correction whose SIGN and MOVE differ (SCAN 1 reeve_mono cools+desaturates a yellow colour print; SCAN 2 quarry_mono warms a cool true-B&W; SCAN 3 draper_mono desaturates out the original sepia; SCAN 4 market_mono recovers flat contrast; SCAN 5 canal_mono neutralises+desaturates a faded colour, consuming the step-3 cropped output). The SHARED house tone is then applied identically by image_apply_monochromatic_tint to each neutral base (9 reeve_toned, 10 quarry_toned, 11 draper_toned, 12 market_toned, 13 canal_toned) — the desaturate-before-tone order is a dependent step. The featured hero forks: market_toned (12) feeds both its master (18) and the cutout remove_background({backgroundColor cream}) (14) -> cameo resize (20).
